mensajes.asunto: Phase two — scope for the board
mensajes.cuerpo:
Daniela,

Here is the phase-two scope on two fronts, as we agreed: (1) the shift assistant for the 38 supervisors, with the line-stop data; (2) the weekly dashboard for you and Rodrigo. The quality-photos stream stays out until the floor has lighting.

Phase-one numbers for the board: 31 of 38 supervisors used it last week, 2.3 queries per shift, and the line-stop report went from 40 minutes to 6.

If the board remembers one thing, make it this: the assistant adapts to the supervisor, not the other way around.

Best,
Pablo

mensajes.asunto: RE: Phase two — scope for the board
mensajes.cuerpo:
Pablo, thanks for the document. I present it in two days, and the board asked me two questions I couldn't answer:

1. Who owns the data after phase two? Rodrigo wants it in writing that everything that goes into the assistant belongs to Ferra, and that if we stop working with you, we take it with us.

2. What happens if the supervisors stop using it? It already happened to us with the maintenance system in 2023. They want to know what you do when usage drops, not just what the software does.

If you can answer before then, even better. The board meets at 9.

Best,
Daniela

mensajes.asunto: Supervisors who use the tool, not the other way around
mensajes.cuerpo:
Jonah,

You wrote on LinkedIn that your plant bought two AI tools nobody uses. I've had the opposite result at a 200-person plant in Monterrey — 31 of 38 supervisors active last week — and the difference was not the software.

Happy to tell you what we did in a 15-minute call. If it doesn't apply to a food plant, you'll know in five.

Pablo

mensajes.asunto: Re: Supervisors who use the tool, not the other way around
mensajes.cuerpo:
Pablo, what was the difference? Give me the short version here and I'll decide if the call is worth it.

Jonah

mensajes.asunto: Re: Supervisors who use the tool, not the other way around
mensajes.cuerpo:
Short version: we trained the tool on how each supervisor already reports a line stop, instead of training the supervisors on the tool. Three weeks in the plant, no slides. The AI adapts to the worker, not the worker to the AI.

If that's the kind of thing you want for your plant, any afternoon in the next three days works for a call.

Pablo
